title: The normalized finite exceptional system descends for specified dualities
statement: Fix D,l,Omega as in [def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data], separated finite-type D.k-schemes X,Y, a separated finite-type D.k-morphism f:X to Y, a compactification c, and specified Dualities BX and BY with all their finite-origin equations. There exists Exceptional A for this compactification: its system is a single finite rational exceptional system at the auxiliary small closure, its left and right functors retain the literal stage, its stage comparisons have identity components, and its actual adjunction unit, counit and scalar squares have the required finite components. Moreover ExceptionalFormula BX BY c A is nonempty: A.right is canonically BY.dual.rightOp followed by pullback.op and BX.dual, normalized to the RationalOperations.ExceptionalIdentification for these same finite dualities.

proof.text: Take the single exceptional system from RationalOperations at the auxiliary small closure and use only its finite rational fields. Its scalar cocycle and identity formulas, together with the canonical scalar associator normalization, define coherent morphisms of the actual X and Y stage systems. Their descended object maps retain the coefficient stage and yield identity inclusion comparisons.

The finite scalar comparison is the adjunction mate, so the finite units and counits form compatible natural-transformation families. Apply compatible-unit-and-counit adjunction descent. Its explicit components give every required unit, counit and scalar equation in ExceptionalProperties.

At each field identify the specified rational dualities with the canonical finite internal-Hom descriptions by uniqueness of the normalized evaluation transpose. Transport the rational exceptional comparison through those identifications. Its scalar squares and those of pullback make it and its inverse compatible families. Descend them to inverse natural transformations. The published pullback object formula and the given BX and BY inclusion comparisons give exactly ExceptionalFormula.normalized.
